title: ～上に — “in addition to ～ / on top of that”
summary: Adds one more fact to what was said first: “not only A, but also B.” It attaches to the plain form of a verb or adjective, or noun + の / な-adjective + な. A and B are usually both good or both bad.

patterns.form: 動詞・い形容詞 普通形＋上に
patterns.gloss: plain form + 上に (e.g. 広い上に, 混んでいた上に)

patterns.form: な形容詞（な）／名詞（の）＋上に
patterns.gloss: 静かな上に, 雨の上に

body.p: A上にB means “A is the case, and on top of that B too.” 広い上に、明るい: spacious, and bright as well. A and B are usually the same kind of evaluation (both positive or both negative).
Plain form of verbs and い-adjectives: 安い上に, 降った上に. な-adjectives take な: 便利な上に. Nouns take の: 雨の上に. Both past and non-past can be used.
～だけでなく～も is the plain version. ～上に is slightly formal and often used for reasons or evaluations. Adding ～まで (as in 雨まで降ってきた) strengthens the “even worse” feeling.

examples.ja: この部屋（へや）は広（ひろ）い上（うえ）に、明（あか）るい。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa hiroi ue ni, akarui.
examples.tr: This room is spacious, and on top of that, bright.

examples.ja: 今日（きょう）は道（みち）が混（こ）んでいた上（うえ）に、雨（あめ）まで降（ふ）ってきた。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa michi ga konde ita ue ni, ame made futte kita.
examples.tr: Today the roads were crowded, and on top of that it started to rain.

examples.ja: この仕事（しごと）は給料（きゅうりょう）が安（やす）い上（うえ）に、休（やす）みも少（すく）ない。
examples.romaji: Kono shigoto wa kyuuryou ga yasui ue ni, yasumi mo sukunai.
examples.tr: This job pays little, and in addition there are few days off.

pitfalls: Do not mix good and bad: “cheap, and also the quality is bad” is unnatural with 上に. Keep A and B in the same direction.
Do not confuse 上に with 上で (“after ～”). They have different meanings.
